name: When is custom molding necessary instead of standard stock trim?

mainEntity.name: When is custom molding necessary instead of standard stock trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom molding is recommended when off-the-shelf trim profiles fail to match existing historic millwork, when ceilings require multi-piece builds, or when settling has caused significant wall wave. Standard stock trim purchased from big-box stores comes in limited dimensions that often appear undersized in updated kitchens or renovated basements. Furthermore, older properties across Denver and Englewood often have plaster walls or non-standard jamb depths where standard factory casings leave visible gaps. Custom molding allows for hand-scribed baseboards, custom backer blocks, and balanced transitions around cabinetry, fireplace mantels, and floor-to-ceiling tile borders.
acceptedAnswer.description: Custom molding is needed when matching historic trim, framing tall ceilings, dressing custom cabinetry, or fitting walls where stock trim leaves gaps or looks undersized.
